subject: No-learn evidence sprint, EU residency & subprocessor map
messages:
From: Ari Levin <ari.levin@medsys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: No-learn evidence pack and cross-border questions

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and security have a few follow-ups before we can sign the Dedicated commitment: primarily we need firm evidence that customer data will not be used to improve models (no-learn / no-train), a current roster of subprocessors (including any third parties used for logging/observability), and confirmation of legal transfer mechanisms for EU data (SCCs or equivalent).

Attached is a short questionnaire (MedSys-Questionnaire.xlsx) that outlines the specific items we need. In particular:
- Contractual amendment (DPA markup) reflecting the no-learn commitment — do you have standard language?
- Proof that prompt/response ownership remains with MedSys and that Redwood won’t claim derivative rights.
- Evidence of recent access logs/audit for subprocessors (last 90 days) or an auditor contact we can use.
- Clarify where inference copies / logs may be stored and whether they transfer to the US.

Can we do a short evidence sprint next week (3–5 business days) to assemble the pack? Procurement would also like a DocuSign-ready amendment if possible.

Thanks,
Ari Levin
Head of IT Security
MedSys Health
ari.levin@medsys.com

Subject: Re: No-learn evidence pack and cross-border questions

Hi Ari —

Appreciate the detailed list. We can absolutely run a focused evidence sprint and produce an evidence pack that covers: the signed no-learn commitment, subprocessor roster, KM/crypto posture notes, and audit logs where available.

Quick notes / proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm scope and who at MedSys will be the reviewer (procurement contact + security).
- Wed–Thu: Redwood compiles artifacts (contract template, roster CSV, logs export sample, KMS/SCC notes).
- Fri: handover via secure Drive link + optional Zoom walkthrough.

I've attached our no-learn commitment template (redwood-no-learn-commitment-template.pdf) and the current subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_20270614.csv) for your review. Jonas (legal) and Neha (AM / procurement lead) are looped for questions and the DocuSign flow.

If MedSys requires the amendment to be executed before pilot activation, we can prioritize the DPA markup; otherwise, we can provide a draft and a DocuSign link alongside the evidence.

Would Monday 21 Jun at 11:00 UTC work for a kickoff?

Best,

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ari Levin <ari.levin@medsys.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: No-learn evidence pack and cross-border questions

Vanessa / Neha —

Quick legal notes for the evidence pack:
1) No-learn/no-train: we have a short amendment that binds Redwood (and subprocessors) to not use customer-provided input/output for model improvement. I attached a working copy to the internal folder. For execution we can either append to the DPA or present as a standalone schedule.
2) Subprocessors & access logs: we can provide the roster CSV (attached) and a redacted sample of recent access logs (timestamps + role/host) for the last 90 days. We should not leak token contents — logs will show metadata and operation types.
3) Cross-border: for EU-origin data we rely on SCCs + customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) if requested; note that some telemetry for routing/metrics is aggregated and does not contain PII. If MedSys requires a data residency guarantee (no egress from EU), we need to scope that as a Dedicated configuration and confirm infra placement.
4) Procurement wants evidence; procurement usually accepts a signed amendment + evidence pack. If they insist on an auditor, we can provide an auditor contact (auditor@trustfirm.io) and set up a limited evidence access bucket.

Action items: Vanessa to confirm whether we should push signed amendment via DocuSign or initial draft for comment. Neha to manage procurement timeline.

J

--
Jonas Weber
Counsel — Redwood Inference

Vanessa / team —

Thanks, that plan sounds good. A couple clarifications from procurement/security:
- We do want an executed DPA amendment referencing the no-learn commitment before we route production data to Dedicated. Markup attached (see MedSys-Questionnaire.xlsx tab 4).
- Export control: confirm if any telemetry or logs are mirrored to US-based support teams. If so, we need confirmatory language or a mitigation plan.
- Auditor: please send the onboarding contact and the scope (read-only access to the evidence folder + timeline). Our auditor is available the week of 21 Jun.

Ari / team —

Thanks — next steps and deliverables below. We’ll treat this as an evidence sprint (scope limited to the items in your questionnaire).

Deliverables (expected by 2027-06-18 EOD unless otherwise noted):
- Signed no-learn amendment (we’ll prepare and send DocuSign link): https://docusign.net/link/placeholder/MS-4672-DPA-amend
- Evidence pack (secure Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/MS-4672/evidence-pack — will include redwood-no-learn-commitment-template.pdf, subprocessor_roster_20270614.csv, a redacted logs sample, and SCC/KMS notes (sccs-and-kms-notes.docx).
- Auditor contact: TrustFirm — auditor@trustfirm.io (read-only onboarding; they can be provisioned access to the evidence Drive for independent review).

Operational clarifications:
- Telemetry: routing/metrics are aggregated and do not contain prompt/response content. Copies of prompts/responses are not used for model training in any hosted or Dedicated mode when the no-learn amendment is in place.
- Residency: For EU-only residency we will deploy Dedicated capacity in the EU region; this requires a short infra configuration step prior to production. If MedSys requests enforced residency, we’ll add the residency clause to the amendment and confirm the infra cutover date.

Kickoff: Monday 21 Jun 2027 at 11:00 UTC (Zoom invite to follow).

If procurement needs the signed amendment earlier, let me know and we’ll prioritize execution.

Thanks,
